$comment: thegn control API v1 wire contract — generated; regenerate with THEGN_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test -p thegn-svc --test control_schema

AgentLaunch.description:
Launch a configured agent in a worktree.

The point of this type is that a supervisor should say *what it wants*, not reconstruct how thegn launches things. Given an `[[agents]]` name it gets the worktree's sandbox, the bundle/identity environment, the provider credential directory (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and friends), the resource cap, and the `worktrees.agent` binding — all the machinery an interactive pane already goes through, none of which a raw `argv` can reach.

agent.description: An `[[agents]]`/`[[tools]]` name, or — when no entry is named that — a provider id from thegn's provider registry (`claude`, `codex`), so a supervisor need not know the operator's entry names. Anything else is an error rather than a guess.

bind_worktree.description: Record this agent as the worktree's own (`worktrees.agent`), so resurrection relaunches it and the sidebar attributes its activity.

continue_last.description: Continue the harness's own most recent session in the worktree — the id-free relaunch form the transport-retry observer uses (THE-86). Resolved through [`thegn_core::harness::Harness::continue_command`]; a harness without a continue form refuses, exactly like an unsupported `resume`. Wire-additive with a `false` default: older clients are unaffected.

headless.description: Run headlessly (`claude -p …`) rather than as an interactive TUI. Defaults to headless exactly when a prompt is given.

prompt.description: The task to seed the first turn with. Empty ⇒ launch interactively.

resume.description: Resume a prior harness session by id instead of launching cold. The id is untrusted input (it crosses MCP/HTTP/CLI): it is validated against the harness's discovered-id shape and refused if it fails, never interpolated raw. A harness without resume support, or an empty id, launches normally. See [`thegn_core::harness`].

stage.description: A `[[pipeline.stages]]` name whose `model` / `env` / `permissions` overrides are layered over the agent entry for this launch — how one entry runs a cheap tier for coders and a strong one for reviewers. Unknown stage ⇒ error. See `thegn_core::agent_task::effective_agent`.

AttachKind.description: How a client attaches. `Observer` never resizes the PTY and never holds the relay lease open (read-mostly thin clients); `Interactive` is the compositor/CLI case — last interactive writer wins resizes.

BrowserCommand.description: The preview-browser verb payload — defined now so the contract is stable; v1 always answers [`ControlError::Unimplemented`].

DispatchPutReq.description:
The `dispatches.put` verb payload (THE-57): one row appended to the roster.

The four pipeline fields (v56) are optional and default-absent, so a caller written against the three-string version keeps working unchanged. `put` carries them all: the roster gains columns, not verbs — there is deliberately no `dispatches.update`, because a mutable stage field invites thegn to become the thing that advances it.

artifact_path.description: Path to the handoff artifact committed in the worktree. A pointer, never the payload.

parent_id.description: The roster row this one was chunked out of (architect → coder fan-out).

session_id.description: The daemon session running this dispatch — the row's identity for pane-exit attribution when several stages share one worktree.

stage.description: Which `[[pipeline.stages]]` step this row is. Stored and grouped by; never advanced by thegn.

GitFileStatus.description: One changed file in a worktree (the mobile stage/commit contract).

OpenSpec.description:
What to run when opening a fresh session.

`Default` exists so callers can spread `..Default::default()` and pick up new optional fields without a construction-site sweep — the three added for agent launch cost exactly that sweep, and there will be more.

adopt.description: Also file an `adopt_session` intent, so a running compositor grafts this session into a real pane instead of leaving it headless.

agent.description:
Launch a configured agent instead of a raw `argv`.

With this set the daemon resolves the command, the sandbox and the environment itself — the same composition an interactive pane gets — so a caller does not have to know how to build any of it. `argv` is then ignored and may be empty.

already_capped.description:
The caller already CPU-capped `argv`.

The compositor does: it wraps via `sandbox::enter_argv` before building this spec, so the daemon must not wrap a second time. Everyone else leaves this `false` and gets the cap applied for them.

worktree.description: Worktree this session belongs to (listing/grouping hint).

PrStatusRow.description: One worktree's cached PR facts (the `pr.status` verb). Projected from the daemon's `pr_cache` table — a TTL'd read-through cache of the forge's answer, so `fetched_at` tells the client how stale the row is (the forge itself stays the source of truth).

fetched_at.description: Unix seconds the cache row was fetched at.

worktree.description: Absolute worktree path the PR is cached for.

body.description: Lossy UTF-8 rendering of at most `[preview] max_body_bytes` bytes.

console_errors.description: Bounded, redacted error-shaped lines from the associated dev-server pane.

diagnostics_source.description: `dev-server-pane` when those diagnostics were available, otherwise `unavailable`.

status.description: Origin server HTTP status, preserved as data (including non-2xx).

PreviewFetchRequest.description: A bounded, credential-free preview fetch request.

include_console.description: Include bounded, redacted dev-server pane error lines. This is not a browser JavaScript-console claim.

url.description: Absolute `http`/`https` URL. The host applies its loopback policy before connecting and again after every redirect.

worktree.description: Optional worktree identity used only to select pane diagnostics.

PushedNote.description: The `notify.push` verb payload — a desktop-notification-shaped note pushed into the tray over the API (the wire mirror of `thegn notify push`).

body.description: Longer detail, appended to the inbox message when non-empty.

source.description: Opaque source reference stored on the row; defaults to `"api"`.

title.description: Short summary line (the inbox message when `body` is empty).

urgency.description: `"alert"`/`"critical"` raise the red-flag priority; anything else (or absent) lands at the normal notice tier.

RecordSpec.description: The `sessions.record` request: what to do with a session's recording. The daemon owns the file, so a start returns the path but the caller never receives contents over the wire.

oneOf.description: Begin recording this session's PTY output to a fresh `.cast` file.
Stop and finalize the current recording.
Report the recording state without changing it.

RecordStatus.description: The `sessions.record` response: the recording state after the operation.

bytes.description: Bytes written to the cast file so far.

capped.description: Set when the recording stopped because it reached `[recording] max_bytes` (the file is finalized and valid; the session was unaffected).

path.description: The on-disk path of the (active or just-finalized) `.cast` file, if any. A path is a locator for audit — the contents are never returned.

recording.description: Whether a recording is currently active.

truncated.description: `Some(reason)` when the recording could NOT be finalized cleanly (the final write or flush failed — a full disk, a quota). The `.cast` at `path` is short of the session's last output, so a client must report it as truncated rather than saved. `None` on every healthy path.

SessionInfo.description:
One daemon-owned session (= one PTY + emulator). The compositor's tab/pane layout stays client-side; the daemon's registry is flat.

`Default` is for construction sites (mostly tests) that care about a few fields — see the note on [`OpenSpec`].

error_active.description: Whether the live session currently has a harness-level error banner. This is included in session listings so a new event subscriber can bootstrap its cache before consuming activity deltas.

exit_code.description: The finished child's exit code, when it exited and could be reaped.

exited_at_ms.description:
Set when this row is a session that has **finished** and is still being held readable (see the daemon's tombstones). `None` means live.

A supervisor polling its fleet needs "which of my workers are done" to be answerable in one call, and a worker that exited thirty seconds ago must not simply vanish from the roster — that is the same lost-result race the tombstones exist to close, one level up.

final_state.description: The agent state this session held at the moment it finished (`blocked` · `working` · `done` · `idle`). `None` for a live session — ask `wait`, or read the `Activity` feed, for that.

lease_expires_at.description: Set while a relay lease is keeping this detached session warm.

pid.description: The PTY child's pid on the daemon's host. A same-host compositor uses it for `/proc`-based cwd/foreground-command capture at persist time.

recording.description: Set while (or just after) this session is being recorded as an asciicast: the on-disk path of the `.cast` file. The API returns the path so a client can audit and locate the recording — never its contents. `None` when nothing is being recorded.

worktree.description: Worktree hint (path) when the session was opened for one.

SessionRecord.description: One discovered session, as `agent.sessions` projects it. Assembled by the svc walker from a [`SessionLayout`] match plus a [`SessionSummary`] parse.

summary.description: A truncated one-line summary — never transcript bodies or credentials.

unlinked.description: `true` when the session's worktree is not one thegn tracks (harness stores are host-wide; toktrack/codeg show the host-wide view is expected).

SplitDir.description: Where a `split` places the new pane relative to the target session. Mirrors the compositor's `center::Dir`; the wire type lives here so `thegn-svc` does not depend on `thegn-host`.

oneOf.description: New pane to the right (vertical divider).

WaitCondition.description:
A condition for the agent-driving `wait` verb: block until a session reaches a state instead of polling it.

The activity-derived conditions (`Idle`/`Blocked`/`Done`) are the pane daemon's per-session observer of the activity FSM, projected through `thegn_core::attention::pane_agent_state`; `OutputMatches` scans the session's ANSI-stripped scrollback. **A session that has exited resolves every condition** as `exited` with its code rather than hanging or 404ing — nothing ever waits on a corpse (see the daemon's tombstones).

oneOf.description: The agent went idle after being active (finished a turn).
The agent is blocked waiting on the user (asked for input).
The session's output matched this regex.

WaitOutcome.description: The result of a `wait`: `matched=false` means the timeout elapsed first.

condition.description: Which condition fired (or the one waited on, if timed out).

exit_code.description: The PTY exit code, when the condition was `Exited`.

WorktreeCreateReq.description: The `worktrees.create` verb payload (THE-57). Creates a worktree, optionally from a tracker issue — deriving the branch from the issue's provider hint and linking the issue to the new worktree — the headless twin of the `D` key's dispatch pipeline, sharing the same branch-derivation rule so the two cannot drift.

branch.description: Explicit branch name. Overrides issue-hint derivation when set.

issue.description: Tracker issue id (`"<provider>:<key>"`). When given and `branch` is empty, the branch derives from the issue's `branch_hint` (naming fallback otherwise) and the issue is linked to the new worktree.

repo.description: A path inside the repo to anchor to (any worktree of it). Empty ⇒ the daemon resolves the repo from its own cwd.

WorktreeInfo.description: One worktree registered with thegn (the `worktrees.list` capability). A wire type, not the DB row: clients see what they can act on, not sort keys and tab names.

location.description: Remote-location descriptor (JSON) for a remote worktree; empty = local.
